subject: Chemistry
title: How Sunscreen Protects Skin
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Sunscreen Protects Skin.

hook.text: Sunscreen contains molecules that absorb ultraviolet light and convert it harmlessly into heat.

buildup.text: UV rays from the Sun damage DNA in skin cells. This damage can cause sunburn and skin cancer.

discovery.text: Chemical sunscreens like avobenzone absorb UV photons. Their electrons get excited, then release energy as heat.

twist.text: Mineral sunscreens (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) work differently—they scatter and reflect UV like tiny mirrors.

climax.text: SPF 30 blocks 97% of UVB rays. SPF 50 blocks 98%. The difference is smaller than most people think.

punchline.text: Absorb UV, release heat. Molecules that take the bullet for your DNA.

quiz.question: How do chemical sunscreens protect your skin?
options: They absorb UV photons and release the energy as harmless heat
They reflect all sunlight away from the skin
They thicken the outer layer of skin

details.summary: Sunscreens contain chemical or mineral filters that protect skin from ultraviolet radiation. Chemical filters like avobenzone absorb UV photons and release the energy as heat. Mineral filters like zinc oxide and titanium dioxide physically scatter and reflect UV rays away from the skin surface.
details.whyItMatters: UV radiation causes DNA damage that leads to skin cancer and premature aging. Sunscreen chemistry is a critical public health tool that prevents millions of skin cancer cases worldwide.
takeaways: Chemical sunscreens absorb UV and release the energy as harmless heat
Mineral sunscreens scatter and reflect UV away from skin
Broad-spectrum protection requires blocking both UVA and UVB radiation

faq.question: What is the difference between UVA and UVB protection in sunscreen?
faq.answer: UVB causes sunburn and direct DNA damage, while UVA penetrates deeper and causes premature aging and indirect DNA damage. Most early sunscreens only blocked UVB. Modern broad-spectrum sunscreens block both, using multiple active ingredients to cover the full UV spectrum.

faq.question: Do chemical sunscreens actually damage coral reefs?
faq.answer: Research shows that oxybenzone and octinoxate can bleach coral and harm marine larvae at high concentrations. Hawaii and Palau have banned these ingredients in sunscreens. Mineral sunscreens with zinc oxide are considered reef-safe alternatives, though no sunscreen is completely inert in ecosystems.
